exposure: Bone cancer subtypes: osteosarcoma (OS), Ewing Sarcoma (ES), and chondrosarcoma (CS)
outcome: Risk of bone cancer subtypes (OS, ES, CS)
cohort: Cases of bone cancer (n=914) and matched controls (n=9140) in Norway, Sweden, and Denmark born between 1970 and 2010
finding: The study found limited evidence for a significant role of pregnancy factors in the development of bone cancers, although higher maternal education was associated with an increased risk of osteosarcoma.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with a 29% risk reduction for osteosarcoma.
birth_weight: Assessed but no association found with any bone tumor subtypes
